title: Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB)
subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
summary: HMB is menstrual loss that interferes with quality of life. Check FBC in all, start drug treatment without investigation when risk of pathology is low, offer an LNG-IUS first line, otherwise tranexamic acid, NSAIDs, combined hormonal contraception or cyclical progestogen; use hysteroscopy or ultrasound when structural or endometrial pathology is suspected.

sections.title: Recognise and assess
items: HMB: excessive menstrual blood loss that interferes with physical, social, emotional or material quality of life. Aim to improve quality of life rather than measured blood loss.

History: nature of bleeding; intermenstrual or postcoital bleeding; pelvic pain or pressure (fibroids, adenomyosis, polyps, endometrial pathology); impact; comorbidities; previous treatment; contraceptive and fertility wishes.

Classify causes with FIGO PALM-COEIN: structural (polyp, adenomyosis, leiomyoma, malignancy or hyperplasia) and non-structural (coagulopathy, ovulatory dysfunction, endometrial, iatrogenic, not yet classified).

HMB without other symptoms can be treated with drugs without examination, unless an LNG-IUS is chosen. Examine (abdominal, speculum and bimanual) if there are related symptoms and before any investigation or LNG-IUS fitting.
Exclude pregnancy in every woman of reproductive age.

sections.title: Investigations
items: FBC for all women with HMB, alongside treatment; treat iron deficiency.

Test for a coagulation disorder (for example von Willebrand disease) if HMB since menarche and the personal or family history suggests a bleeding disorder. Do not test female hormones; test thyroid only with clinical features.
Low risk of fibroids, cavity abnormality, histological abnormality or adenomyosis: start drug treatment without further investigation.

Outpatient hysteroscopy if history suggests submucosal fibroids, polyps or endometrial pathology (persistent intermenstrual bleeding or risk factors). Take an endometrial biopsy at hysteroscopy if high risk; do not do a blind biopsy.
High risk of endometrial pathology: persistent intermenstrual or irregular bleeding, infrequent heavy bleeding with obesity or PCOS, tamoxifen use, or failed treatment.

Pelvic ultrasound if the uterus is palpable abdominally, a pelvic mass is suspected or examination is difficult; transvaginal ultrasound for significant dysmenorrhoea or a bulky tender uterus (adenomyosis). Do not use MRI, saline sonography or D and C first line.

sections.title: No pathology, fibroids under 3 cm, or adenomyosis
items: First line: LNG-IUS (52 mg) for no identified pathology, fibroids under 3 cm that do not distort the cavity, or suspected or confirmed adenomyosis.
Explain that irregular bleeding is expected in the first cycles and may last beyond 6 months; allow at least 6 cycles to judge benefit.

If an LNG-IUS is declined or unsuitable: non-hormonal tranexamic acid or an NSAID (taken only during menstruation, and can be combined), or hormonal combined hormonal contraception or cyclical oral progestogen.
Progestogen-only contraception (DMPA, implant, desogestrel) may suppress periods. Continue tranexamic acid or NSAIDs for as long as they help.
Non-hormonal options (tranexamic acid, NSAIDs) suit women trying to conceive.

sections.title: Fibroids 3 cm or more, and treatment failure
items: Refer for specialist assessment. While waiting, offer tranexamic acid and/or NSAIDs.

Options by size, site, number and symptoms: tranexamic acid, NSAIDs, LNG-IUS, CHC, cyclical progestogen, GnRH antagonist combinations (relugolix CT, linzagolix), uterine artery embolisation, myomectomy or hysterectomy. Submucosal fibroids: hysteroscopic removal.

Ulipristal acetate 5 mg only for intermittent treatment in premenopausal women when surgery and embolisation are unsuitable, declined or have failed, because of serious liver injury: check liver function before, monthly for the first 2 courses, and before each course.
Failed drug treatment or severe symptoms: refer for second-generation endometrial ablation or hysterectomy. After ablation, avoid pregnancy and use effective contraception.

Consider GnRH analogue pretreatment before hysterectomy or myomectomy if fibroids enlarge or distort the uterus. Do not offer D and C as treatment; remove ovaries at hysterectomy only with express informed consent.

sections.title: Escalate
items: Very heavy ongoing bleeding, haemodynamic instability or symptomatic anaemia: resuscitate, check Hb, group and save and pregnancy test, and arrange same-day gynaecology review.
Suspected cancer (for example postmenopausal bleeding or a suspicious cervix or mass): refer on the urgent suspected cancer pathway.
Treatment unsuccessful, symptoms severe, or woman declines drug treatment: refer to specialist care for investigation and further options.

sections.title: Special considerations
items: Adolescents with HMB since menarche: screen for a bleeding disorder, especially von Willebrand disease.
Tranexamic acid: avoid with active thromboembolic disease or previous venous or arterial thrombosis; reduce the dose in renal impairment.
NSAIDs: avoid with active peptic ulcer, significant renal impairment or NSAID-sensitive asthma.
India: iron deficiency anaemia is very common; check Hb (and ferritin where available) and give oral iron alongside HMB treatment. The approach otherwise follows NICE NG88.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Blind endometrial biopsy instead of hysteroscopy-directed sampling in women at risk of endometrial pathology.
Missing pregnancy, cervical pathology or infection as the cause of irregular bleeding.
Routine hormone or thyroid tests that do not change management.
Ignoring iron deficiency while treating the bleeding.
Giving tranexamic acid to a woman with previous VTE.

drugs.name: Tranexamic acid
drugs.dose: 1 g orally three times daily for up to 4 days per cycle, starting at the onset of bleeding (maximum 4 g per day)
drugs.notes: Non-hormonal. Avoid with active or previous thromboembolism; reduce dose in renal impairment.

drugs.name: Mefenamic acid
drugs.dose: 500 mg orally three times daily from the first day of bleeding until heavy bleeding settles
drugs.notes: NSAID; also relieves dysmenorrhoea. Avoid with peptic ulcer or renal impairment.

drugs.name: Levonorgestrel intrauterine system
drugs.notes: First line for HMB without significant pathology. Replace according to the product licence.

drugs.name: Combined oral contraceptive
drugs.dose: Monophasic COC (for example ethinylestradiol 30 micrograms with levonorgestrel 150 micrograms) daily; packets can be taken back to back
drugs.notes: Check medical eligibility (UKMEC or WHO MEC) first.

drugs.name: Norethisterone (cyclical)
drugs.dose: 5 mg orally three times daily from day 5 to day 26 of the cycle
drugs.notes: Cyclical oral progestogen; not a reliable contraceptive.

drugs.name: Ulipristal acetate (fibroids)
drugs.dose: 5 mg orally once daily in intermittent courses of up to 3 months (up to 4 courses)
drugs.notes: Only when surgery and embolisation are unsuitable or failed. Liver function before, monthly for the first 2 courses, and before each course.
